newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU asks Bonn to recoup millions of marks in duties.
newsitem.headline: EU asks Bonn to recoup millions of marks in duties.

text.p: The European Commission told Germany on Wednesday to recover more than 10 million marks ($5.9 million) in unpaid duties on imports of Turkish television sets.
The decision follows complaints from rival manufacturers that TV sets entered Germany at abnormally low prices between 1991 and 1994.
At issue was Turkey's apparent failure to levy a customs duty on imports of components used in the manufacture of television sets intended for the EU market.

Under a preferential agreement with the 15-nation bloc, Turkish televisions may be exempted from import duty when entering the EU, but only if tariffs due on components bought in third countries have been paid.
This did not happen in seven individual cases, the Commission said in a statement, with the result that the customs duty was then due on the full value of the sets.

It rejected German importers' claim that "they acted in good faith", and warned that it would be taking steps to avoid such fraudulent practices in relation with other bilateral preferential agreements.

"We must protect the financial interests of the Union and, at the same time, enable traders to operate within a clear, controllable framework," Mario Monti, EU commissioner in charge of customs, said in the statement.
The unfairly low-priced sets are said to have harmed sales in Germany of Grundig, its Dutch parent Philips and France's Thomson, an industry source said on Tuesday.
